summary: 3D layout-controlled image editing gives users explicit control over object placement and camera viewpoint. In a sequence of edits, however, the latest image can lose the appearance of an object when it is occluded or leaves view.
takeaways: Geometry-Aligned Memory Conditioning supplies the retrieved tokens to a FLUX.2 editor using target-view positions, shared box-local embeddings, and object-wise attention.
Box-Surface Latent Memory retains image latents on box faces and retrieves them along rays in the target view.
A correspondence loss encourages the editor to attend to matching observations during denoising.
